newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Innovest says has Congo timber deals.
newsitem.headline: Innovest says has Congo timber deals.

text.p: Malaysian property developer and timber company Innovest Bhd said on Monday it has signed agreements with the Congo government to acquire two timber concession areas for $2.34 million.
The concession agreements on the 831,821-acre lands in south western Congo include a timber extraction permit, Innovest said in a statement.
The company would incorporate a Congolese subsidiary, Innovest Congo S.A., to take over and operate the concession for a period of 25 years.
Innovest plans to hold 95 percent equity in Innovest Congo with the remaining five percent offered to the state government of Mossendjo.
"The Congolose government has also agreed to provide Innovest Congo S.A. with tax exemption during the first five years of its operation and other incentives on machinery investment," Innovest said.
In the same statement, Innovest said it has signed an agreement with the Malaysian state government of Perak to develop a beach front area of 10,000 acres.
Development is planned for 20 years, with the first five years for land reclamation work and the balance for construction.
Both projects would be financed through internally generated funds.
